# VRFBuildProfiles

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Core.Editors.Build` · assembly `VRFramework.Core.Editors` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/interaction/physics-hold/Editor/Build/VRFBuildProfiles.cs#L17)

The framework's dealings with Unity's build profiles, in one place.

VRF settings ride along on a profile as a component, which Unity stores as a sub-asset of
the profile asset. `CreateComponent`hides what it creates, because Unity's own
components are only ever meant to be reached through the Build Profiles window; ours is
unhidden so it can be selected under its profile in the Project window and edited like
any other asset.

### Normalize(VRFBuildSettings) {#normalize-vrfbuildsettings}

Brings a settings object up to what the framework expects, whichever route created it.

Unity's "Add Settings" menu builds the component itself: it hides it, leaves it
unnamed and puts nothing on it. This is what makes one added that way look and
behave like one added from the VRF Build window. Every check is against what is
already there, so a settled object is never marked dirty by being read.

```csharp
public static void Normalize(VRFBuildSettings settings)
```
